title: Clo User Summit: Madrid 2025 🇪🇸💃
description:
Watch the highlights from our CLO User Summit Madrid 2025 💃! A big thank you goes out to all of our speakers, partners, and most of all, all our attendees who joined from over 50 brands and vendors in Spain and Portugal. We can't wait to see you all again next year!

This year, we had an amazing speaker line-up from Joma, Red21, and Pyrenaica, a brand from Corvex Group, and a panel talk on brand and vendor collaboration with FSM, Happypunt, and UNITEKS, representing a larger part of the garment production value chain. Attendees could see firsthand how these brands integrated CLO and 3D to reach new levels of efficiency and creativity throughout the product lifecycle.

Want to check out more Spanish-speaking content? Check out our Spanish YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/@CLOesp/featured

markdown_content: ## Introduction to the Clo User Summit Madrid 2025 This section introduces the purpose of the Clo User Summit held in Madrid, focusing on fostering connections and conversations among professionals in the textile sector, particularly around 3D technology applications in production and confection. The event is designed as a collaborative space for industry professionals to share ideas and experiences. Last year’s summit was successful in bringing together many textile sector experts, which helped inspire new insights, especially related to 3D integration in the industry. Networking at the event is seen as crucial for illuminating challenges and opportunities within textile production. ## Impact of 3D Technology on Textile Production This section covers how 3D technology has influenced company growth, efficiency, and quality in textile manufacturing, highlighting a case study involving Luis’s company. Luis’s initiative demonstrated significant improvements in his company by integrating 3D technology into production processes. The benefits included time savings, economic gains, and enhanced product quality. The use of 3D digital tools allows for a more precise understanding of garment construction, particularly the knit structure, which traditionally depends heavily on the physical net or fabric. Digitizing and creating a comprehensive digital library for confection (garment making) ensures that various garment types can be built with the best possible quality. This approach leverages detailed digital representations to optimize production accuracy and consistency. ## Training and Adaptation Within Textile Companies This section explains the importance of tailored training programs to accommodate diverse employee profiles within textile companies, ensuring effective adoption of new technologies. The company involved has a wide range of employee profiles, requiring a gradual and customized training strategy. By adapting training to the specific needs and skill levels of different team members, the company ensures that no one is left behind in the transition to new digital and 3D methodologies. This supportive approach helps employees adapt, learn, and grow alongside technological advancements, fostering a more innovative and capable workforce.
